title: PMT structure, role descriptions and the commercial management approach
blurb: Explain the purpose of the organizing products, place a delivery model on the thin to thick client range, and link the organizing practice to the principles.
question: Where should the senior supplier's accountability for a carbon reduction target be recorded?

teach.h: Three organizing products, all in the PID
teach.body: Formally: the organizing practice is supported by three management products, held in the project initiation documentation: the project management team structure, the role descriptions and the commercial management approach. In plain English: a chart of who is involved and how they work together, a description of what each role must do, and the rules for buying from and managing suppliers.

teach.body: Ashdown Museum Trust is digitizing its archive. The PMT structure shows executive Moira Grant, senior user Ben Sato (head of collections), senior supplier Kate Rowe (director of the scanning firm), project manager Alex Dunn, and a remote team across two sites. Kate's role description makes her accountable for the supplier's energy-use target. The commercial management approach says procurement will lend two staff (resources) and that the scanning firm delivers all imaging work (delivery model), close to the thin client end.

teach.text: Trap: role descriptions, not the PMT structure, hold specific responsibilities such as accountability for a sustainability target. And the commercial management approach is organizing's approach; the communication and change management approaches belong to the people element, though organizing reviews them at stage boundaries.

items: PMT structure: who is involved, relationships, how they work together.
Role descriptions: PMT roles and specific responsibilities, incl. sustainability accountability.
Commercial management approach: market engagement, procurement, contract management; headings include responsibilities, resources, delivery model.
Thin client = suppliers do most work; thick client = the business does.

summary: You can now explain the purpose of the PMT structure, role descriptions and commercial management approach, place a project on the thin to thick client range, and describe how organizing supports the principles.

A.q: What is the purpose of role descriptions?
options: To show who is involved and how they relate
To set out how supplier contracts are managed
To describe each PMT role and its responsibilities
To describe a product's purpose and specifications
A.why: Role descriptions describe the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities (6.5).

whyNot.0: Who is involved and how they relate is the PMT structure.
whyNot.1: Managing supplier contracts is covered by the commercial management approach.
whyNot.3: A product's purpose and quality specifications are in its product description.

A.q: Which product records who is involved in the project, their relationships and how they will work together?
A.why: The PMT structure sets out who is involved, their relationships and how they will work together.

whyNot.1: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities.
whyNot.2: The commercial management approach covers commercial agreements with suppliers.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers how stakeholders are communicated with.

A.q: Which management approach belongs to the organizing practice?
A.why: The commercial management approach is the organizing practice's management approach.

whyNot.0: The change management approach belongs to the people element.
whyNot.1: The communication management approach belongs to the people element.
whyNot.2: The quality management approach belongs to the quality practice.

B.q: Where should the senior supplier's accountability for a carbon reduction target be recorded?
B.why: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities, including accountability for sustainability targets.

whyNot.0: The PMT structure shows who is involved and how they relate, not specific accountabilities.
whyNot.2: Product descriptions describe products, not people's responsibilities.
whyNot.3: The business case justifies the investment; it does not assign role accountabilities.

B.q:
Which two statements about delivery models are correct?
1. In a thin client model, suppliers do most of the project work.
2. In a thick client model, suppliers also do much of the project management.
3. In a thick client model, the business does most of the work.
4. The delivery model is recorded in the risk management approach.
B.why: Thin client means suppliers do most of the work (1); thick client means the business does most of it (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: suppliers doing much of the management describes a thin client model.
whyNot.2: Both are false: statement 2 describes thin client, and the delivery model sits in the commercial management approach.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the delivery model is part of the commercial management approach.

B.q: Organizing adapts the PMT structure and role descriptions at stage boundaries. Which principle does this apply?
B.why: Organizing applies manage by stages by adapting the PMT structure, role descriptions and related approaches at stage boundaries (tab 6.5).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is applied by using lessons to inform the structure and WBS.
whyNot.1: Tailoring is applied by creating a PMT that fits the project and its people.
whyNot.2: Manage by exception is about tolerances and escalation, not stage-boundary updates.

C.q: A procurement team agrees to provide two of its staff for contract negotiations with a supplier. Which product and heading should record this?
C.why: The commercial management approach records the resources for market engagement, procurement and contract management activities.

whyNot.0: Role descriptions cover PMT roles; the procurement staff provided for contract work are commercial resources.
whyNot.1: The PMT structure shows who is in the PMT and how they work together, not commercial resources.
whyNot.3: The product is right, but the delivery model describes which work suppliers deliver.

C.q: Organizing creates a PMT suited to the project's needs and to the capability of the people involved. Which principle is this, and which product shows the result?
options: Tailor to suit the project; PMT structure
Tailor to suit the project; business case
C.why: Creating a PMT appropriate to the project and the capability of those involved applies tailoring (tab 6.5), and the PMT structure shows it.

whyNot.1: The commercial management approach covers supplier agreements, not the shape of the PMT.
whyNot.2: The principle is right, but the business case does not set out the PMT.

C.q: In which process are the PMT structure and role descriptions first created, and which document later holds them?
options: Initiating a project; the project brief
Starting up a project; the business case
Managing a stage boundary; the PID
Starting up a project; the PID
C.why: They are created in starting up a project (appoint the project management team) and later form part of the PID.

whyNot.0: The project brief is assembled in starting up, before initiation.
whyNot.1: The process is right, but the business case does not hold role descriptions.
whyNot.2: Managing a stage boundary reviews and updates them; they were created in starting up.

reteach.title: A theatre production's paperwork
reteach.question: For a theatre show, which document says who does what, and which says how the costume hire firm is contracted?

blocks.body: The company chart shows who is involved and how they relate (PMT structure). Each person's job sheet lists what they are responsible for, including any green targets (role descriptions). A separate rulebook covers how the costume and lighting firms are chosen, contracted and managed (commercial management approach). If the hire firms make almost everything, that is near the thin client end.

blocks.text: A specific responsibility, such as a sustainability target, goes on the job sheet (role description), not on the chart (PMT structure).

explain.body: Shows who is involved in the project, their relationships and how they will work together, for example co-located or remote working arrangements.

test.q: Which content belongs in the PMT structure?
options: Whether the team is co-located or remote
test.why: The PMT structure covers how people will work together, including co-location or remote working arrangements.

whyNot.0: Specific accountabilities, such as sustainability targets, go in role descriptions.
whyNot.1: Contract management procedures belong in the commercial management approach.
whyNot.3: Quality specifications belong in product descriptions.

explain.body: Describe the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, including accountability for sustainability targets.

test.q: Role descriptions describe the roles of which group?
options: All end users of the products
test.why: Role descriptions cover the roles of those in the project management team.

whyNot.1: Stakeholders without a PMT role are not given role descriptions.
whyNot.2: The business layer is outside the PMT.
whyNot.3: End users are represented by the senior user; they do not each get a role description.

explain.body: Procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities for securing, servicing and maintaining commercial agreements: market engagement, procurement and contract management.

test.q: Which activity does the commercial management approach cover?
test.why: The commercial management approach covers market engagement, procurement and contract management.

whyNot.0: Post-project benefits reviews are planned in the benefits management approach.
whyNot.2: Stakeholder engagement is in the communication management approach.
whyNot.3: Change control is in the issue management approach.

explain.body: Lessons inform the PMT structure and WBS (learn from experience); an explicit structure (define roles); adapt at stage boundaries (manage by stages); a PMT that fits (tailor).

test.q: Using lessons to inform the PMT structure and the WBS applies which principle?
test.why: Organizing applies learn from experience by using lessons to inform the PMT structure, WBS and a healthy project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is applied by adapting the structure at stage boundaries.
whyNot.1: Focus on products is about defining products and product descriptions.
whyNot.2: Tailoring is applied by creating a PMT that suits the project and its people.
